Based upon distribution maps presented in Booth and Wright (1959) only Phlox missoulensis, Rorippa calycina and Aquilegia jonesii occur in south-central Montana. Phlox missoulensis Wherry is a variety of Phlox helseyi Britton belonging to the Phlox family. This species prefers moist, alkaline grassland. It is a tufted woody-based perennial with succulent herbage and white to lilac-colored flowers. Rorippa calycina (Engelm.) Rydb. is a member of the mustard family and is usually found along river banks or in wet soil. It is a perennial plant approximately 0.5 to 1 foot high with yellow flowers or with ascending pods when in fruit. Aquilegia jonesii Parry is a member of the Buttercup family and is commonly known as Jones Columbine. This species is a low-growing perennial plant with basal leaves.
None of these species has been observed on the Project Area and Booth and Wright (1959) indicate that none has been collected in Big Horn County. The only species that may possibly occur at the Project Area is Rorippa calycina, which may occur in favorable habitats along Sarpy Creek or other permanent water sources.
